title: Acceptance tests, not oracles

ground.note: The operator's brief and the decisions settled on 2026-10-27.
The `oracles` lint check, its messages, and the `**Oracle phase:**` / `**Oracle files:**` rules.

context:
phax lets a plan freeze tests before the code exists. One phase writes failing tests from the source spec's acceptance criteria, each behind the test framework's expected-failure marker so the gate stays green. A later phase removes the markers and writes the code, and may not otherwise touch those files. A configured provider judges both gates. phax calls the first phase an oracle phase, its tests oracles, its files oracle files, and says the later phase discharges them.

The name runs through every layer. In plan.md it is the header lines `**Oracle phase:** yes | discharged by phase-NN` and `**Oracle files:** …`, checked by lint's `oracles` check. In phax-plan.json and the plan sidecar it is the phase key `oracle: { dischargedBy, files } | null`. In config it is the `oracles` provider block beside `brief` and `architecture`. Then come the `oracle-request` document on that provider's stdin (verdicts `authored` / `discharged`, keys `oraclePhase`, `oracleCommit`), saved as `checks-attempt-NN.oracle-request.json`, and the gate attribution's appended step with `surface: "oracle"`. Run status has the hold selection `oracle`, and phase status has `oracleStep` on a closed stop. The phase record manifest has the role `oracle` (with `dischargedBy`) or `discharging` (with `oraclePhase`). On the CLI it is `phax run --hold oracle`, `phax resume --skip-oracle` and "Oracle preflight failed", with exit 11. It is also the `## Oracle role` prompt section, the fix-prompt tail, the `oracle.edits.unjudged` telemetry event, the `oracle role` row and the `oracleRole` JSON key of `phax plans overview`, the `oracle` row of `phax records explain`, the `## Oracle pairs` section of the review handoff, `oracle` among a phase record's and a run's verified surfaces, the schemas package's `parseOracleRequest`, the docs page `/guide/oracle-phases`, the `examples/vitest-oracles` example, and four skills.

The test line is `<guarantee> — <size> · <technique> · <oracle> · <oracle | in-phase>[ · <criterion>]`. Its fourth field is what judges the result. Its fifth is the loop that owns the test. The closed technique list is `example, table, property, metamorphic, stateful, fuzz, contract, smoke`. The `phax-review` skill's `wrong-oracle` escape already uses the word in its literature sense.
problem: In testing literature an oracle is the mechanism that decides whether a test passes (Barr, Harman, McMinn, Shahbaz and Yoo, The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey, IEEE TSE 2015). Every test has one, so "oracle phase" does not say what the phase does. What phax does is acceptance test-driven development (Koskela 2007; Pugh 2010; Adzic 2011; the outer loop of Freeman and Pryce 2009): a separate phase writes failing tests from the spec's acceptance criteria, and a later phase makes them pass unchanged. The wrong word now carries two meanings in one test line, where the fourth field is a real oracle and the fifth calls the loop `oracle`. A reader of a plan, a record or the review skill cannot tell which meaning a sentence uses. "Discharge" is jargon that nothing else in testing uses for making a test pass. phax is not at 1.0, so the names can still change without a compatibility layer.

productGoal.statement: Every surface phax ships calls the phase that writes failing tests an acceptance phase, its tests acceptance tests in acceptance test files, and the later phase the one that passes them. The word oracle keeps only its literature meaning: the test line's fourth field, the `wrong-oracle` review escape, and prose about what judges a test. The test line gains one technique, `boundary`. Files a person writes that still use an old name are refused with the new name. Live plan sidecars are lifted by the existing migration, and records already written stay readable.
productGoal.guidingRule: An oracle is what judges a test; an acceptance test is a test written from a spec's acceptance criterion before the code, and phax never uses one word for the other.

terminology.definition: A plan phase that writes failing tests from the source spec's acceptance criteria, each behind the test framework's expected-failure marker. Formerly "oracle phase".

A test written in an acceptance phase and frozen until its passing phase. The name states the test's purpose, checking a specified acceptance criterion, not its size: an acceptance test may be `small`. Formerly "oracle".
The files an acceptance phase declares on its `**Acceptance test files:**` line: the tests and whatever they judge with (generators, tables, fixtures). Formerly "oracle files".
The later phase that removes the expected-failure markers and writes the code so the acceptance tests pass. It "passes" them. Formerly the "discharging phase" that "discharged" them.
An acceptance phase and its passing phase. Formerly "oracle pair".
The command configured under `acceptance` in phax.json or its overlays, which judges both gates of an acceptance pair. Formerly the `oracles` provider.
The gate step phax appends at the gate of each phase of an acceptance pair, which runs the acceptance provider. Formerly the "oracle step".
In the literature sense only: what judges a test's result (an expected value, an invariant, a reference table, a relation between runs, a typed refusal). It is the test line's fourth field.

A test technique: inputs chosen by equivalence partition and boundary value, meaning the empty case, each limit, and just outside each limit. Not the code review's `boundary` lens, which keeps its name.

The code review's `acceptance` lens (each criterion, then its tests) and `boundary` lens (decoding, persisted formats, ports, failures). They keep their ids and meanings, and the code-review answer is not bumped.

Any name in the left column of the rename table (§10, settled), as it appears in a file a person writes, a CLI argument, or a document an earlier release wrote. An answer a provider returns is not such a document: its schema holds only the new names.

requirements.title: Acceptance phase header lines
requirements.statement: WHEN a plan phase's header paragraph carries `**Acceptance phase:** yes` or `**Acceptance phase:** passed by phase-NN` followed by `**Acceptance test files:** <paths>` THE system SHALL read the phase as an acceptance phase whose passing phase is the next phase or phase-NN, applying every rule the `oracles` check applied to oracle phases under the `acceptance` lint check.

requirements.title: Old header lines refused
requirements.statement: IF a plan phase carries a `**Oracle phase:**` or `**Oracle files:**` line THEN the system SHALL report an `acceptance` lint error reading `**Oracle phase:** is no longer read: write **Acceptance phase:**` or `**Oracle files:** is no longer read: write **Acceptance test files:**`, and `phax run` and `phax resume` SHALL refuse the plan with exit 11 and "Acceptance preflight failed".

requirements.title: Acceptance loop
requirements.statement: The system shall read and write a test line's loop as exactly `acceptance` or `in-phase`, with `acceptance` meaning the test is written in an acceptance phase and frozen until its passing phase.

requirements.title: Old loop refused
requirements.statement: IF a test line holds `oracle` in its loop position THEN the system SHALL report a `tests` lint error reading `test line <n> uses the loop 'oracle', which is no longer read: write 'acceptance'`, and SHALL refuse the plan wherever it refuses a departing test line today, before the extraction cache and any model call.

requirements.title: Reserved criterion ids
requirements.statement: IF a plan sidecar or an answer carries a test line whose criterion is `acceptance`, `in-phase` or `oracle` THEN the system SHALL refuse it with `a criterion is neither 'acceptance', 'in-phase' nor 'oracle'`, naming its phase and line.

requirements.title: Boundary technique
requirements.statement: The system shall accept `boundary` as a test technique, placed in the closed list directly after `example`: example, boundary, table, property, metamorphic, stateful, fuzz, contract, smoke.

requirements.title: Acceptance provider
requirements.statement: WHERE a config layer declares `"acceptance": { "command": … }` THE system SHALL run that command as the acceptance step at the gate of every phase of an acceptance pair, exactly as it ran the `oracles` provider.

requirements.title: Old provider key refused
requirements.statement: IF phax.json, phax.local.json or ~/.phax/config.json carries an `oracles` key THEN the system SHALL refuse the configuration with a message naming the file and reading `"oracles" is no longer read: write "acceptance"`.

requirements.title: Hold acceptance phases
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax run --hold acceptance` names a run THE system SHALL hold every acceptance phase of the plan and record the hold selection `acceptance`.

requirements.title: Old hold selection refused
requirements.statement: IF `--hold` is given `oracle`, alone or in a list THEN the system SHALL refuse it before the run is named with `--hold 'oracle' is no longer read: write --hold acceptance`.

requirements.title: Skip the acceptance step
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax resume <run> --skip-acceptance` restarts at a phase of an acceptance pair THE system SHALL record its acceptance step as skipped and still run the configured gate and, when phax.json declares `protectedPaths`, the protected-path check.

requirements.title: Old skip flag refused
requirements.statement: IF `phax resume` is given `--skip-oracle` THEN the system SHALL refuse it with `--skip-oracle is no longer read: write --skip-acceptance`, resuming nothing.

requirements.title: Acceptance request
requirements.statement: The system shall write on the acceptance provider's stdin, and save as `checks-attempt-NN.acceptance-request.json`, an `acceptance-request` document stamped `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/acceptance-request/0.33.0.json`, whose verdict is `authored` or `passed` and whose keys are `phase`, `acceptancePhase`, `base`, `files`, plus `acceptanceCommit` on a `passed` request.

requirements.title: New names in written documents
requirements.statement: The system shall write phax-plan, plan-document, phax-plan-extraction, run-status, phase-status, gate-attribution and phase-record-manifest documents stamped 0.33.0 (from 0.32.0, 0.32.0, 0.32.0, 0.26.0, 0.26.0, 0.31.0 and 0.30.0), carrying only the new names of the rename table: phase key `acceptance: { passedBy, files } | null`, loop `acceptance`, hold selection `acceptance`, stop key `acceptanceStep`, step surface and verified surface `acceptance`, record role `acceptance` with `passedBy` or `passing` with `acceptancePhase`. Every answer schema that carries these names (the plan authoring and decide-handback answer, and the plan-extraction answer) carries only the new ones, every key required and `$schema` a const, and an old name in an answer is refused like any other value outside its enum, never by name.

requirements.title: Records already written stay readable
requirements.statement: WHEN phax or the schemas package reads a record, gate attribution, oracle request, phase status or run status written by an earlier release THE system SHALL read it, presenting its oracle names under the new names of the rename table.

requirements.title: Live plan sidecars lifted
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` runs in a repository with a live plan sidecar below 0.33.0 THE system SHALL rewrite it at 0.33.0 under the new names (phase `acceptance` with `passedBy`, loop `acceptance`), re-render its plan.md header lines, and commit the result.

requirements.title: Unmigrated sidecars refused
requirements.statement: IF a live plan sidecar is below 0.33.0 THEN `phax artifact approve`, `reopen` and `decide` SHALL refuse it with exit 12, naming `phax artifact migrate-documents`.

requirements.title: Archived artifacts untouched
requirements.statement: WHILE a plan or spec lives under an `archive/` folder THE system SHALL leave it as written and keep reading it.

requirements.title: Runs in flight refused
requirements.statement: IF a run's phax-plan.json was extracted by an earlier release THEN `phax resume` and `phax validate --plan` SHALL refuse it, naming `phax archive <run> --force`, while `phax ls` and `phax session-info` still show the run.

requirements.title: Acceptance names in every message
requirements.statement: The system shall name acceptance phases, acceptance tests, acceptance test files, passing phases and the acceptance provider, step and pair in every message, help text, usage contract, prompt section, telemetry event, overview and records row, as the rename table lists.

requirements.title: Oracle in its literature sense only
requirements.statement: The system shall use the word oracle only for the test line's fourth field, the `phax-review` skill's `wrong-oracle` escape, and prose about what judges a test, and shall use the word discharge nowhere, except in the refusals of old names and where it reads or lifts a document written by an earlier release.

requirements.title: The planning skill rewritten
requirements.statement: The bundled phax-planning skill shall teach acceptance phases under an "Acceptance phases" section and an "Acceptance candidate" defaults column. It shall state that acceptance names a test's purpose, not its size, and describe the `boundary` technique.

requirements.title: Upgrade entry
requirements.statement: The upgrading guide shall carry a 0.33.0 entry naming every step an operator takes: the migration, hand-written plans, the phax.json key and its overlays, the `--hold` and `--skip-acceptance` spellings, the acceptance provider's command reading an `acceptance-request`, scripts reading the renamed status, record and overview names or the schemas package's renamed exports, and runs in flight.

nonGoals: Typing the test line's `<oracle>` field, for example with Barr's four kinds (specified, derived, implicit, human): it stays free text.
Any technique beyond `boundary`. Golden or snapshot tests are an oracle (`example · the golden file`), and pairwise and mutation are not wanted now.
Any change to how acceptance phases behave: the pairing rules, markers, gate judgments, holds, stops, resets and refusals stay as they are, under new names.

Rewriting archived plans and specs, briefs under `docs/briefs/`, past release notes under `docs/releases/`, or the upgrading entries of releases before 0.33.0: they record what those releases shipped.

Rewriting the prose of specs and plans under `docs/specs/` and `docs/plans/`: they record decisions in the words of their day. `phax artifact migrate-documents` lifts a live plan sidecar's fields and re-renders what they render; nothing else in an artifact changes.
Rewriting records, gate attributions, oracle requests or status files already written: they are read as they are.
Resuming a run started by an earlier release: it is refused, as it was when 0.32.0 restamped phax-plan.
Recognizing an old name anywhere beyond the refusals this spec lists. An old name is refused with the new name, never accepted as an alias.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Acceptance header lines are read
acceptanceCriteria.given: an `acceptance` provider is configured and a plan's phase-03 carries `**Acceptance phase:** passed by phase-04` and `**Acceptance test files:** `tests/e2e/publish.test.ts``, a file phase-03 plans to create
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax plans lint` runs and the plan is extracted
acceptanceCriteria.then: lint reports no `acceptance` error, and phase-03 in phax-plan.json carries `"acceptance": { "passedBy": "phase-04", "files": ["tests/e2e/publish.test.ts"] }` with `$schema` at 0.33.0

acceptanceCriteria.name: Pairing rules hold under the new names
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan whose phase-03 carries `**Acceptance phase:** discharged by phase-04`, and another whose phase-02 carries `**Acceptance phase:** yes` and no `**Acceptance test files:**` line
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first reports the `acceptance` error `**Acceptance phase:** "discharged by phase-04" is not a declaration: write "yes" or "passed by phase-NN"`, the second `**Acceptance phase:** without **Acceptance test files:**: write both lines or neither`, and both exit 1

acceptanceCriteria.name: Old header lines are refused by name
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan whose phase-03 carries `**Oracle phase:** yes` and `**Oracle files:** `tests/e2e/publish.test.ts``
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax plans lint`, then `phax run --plan`, then `phax resume` of a run started by phax 0.33.0 whose plan.md was later edited back to the old lines, are each run
acceptanceCriteria.then: lint exits 1 with the `acceptance` errors `**Oracle phase:** is no longer read: write **Acceptance phase:**` and `**Oracle files:** is no longer read: write **Acceptance test files:**`, and `phax run` and `phax resume` exit 11 with "Acceptance preflight failed" listing both. A run started before the upgrade never reaches that preflight: `phax resume` refuses it earlier, its phax-plan.json being in the 0.32.0 shape, with the older-phax-plan message naming `phax archive <run> --force`

acceptanceCriteria.name: The acceptance loop
acceptanceCriteria.given: an acceptance phase whose test line is `- every (state, transition) pair is accepted or refused as the table says — small · table · transition table · acceptance · AC-3`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax plans lint` and `phax plans overview` run
acceptanceCriteria.then: lint reports no `tests` error, the extracted test line has `"loop": "acceptance"` and `"oracle": "transition table"`, and the overview's coverage shows AC-3 covered by an `acceptance` line

acceptanceCriteria.name: Loop rules hold under the new names
acceptanceCriteria.given: an ordinary phase with a line in the `acceptance` loop, and an acceptance phase with only `in-phase` lines

Rename table, plan document and phax-plan.json: phase key `oracle` → `acceptance`; `dischargedBy` → `passedBy`; `files` unchanged. plan-document, phax-plan and the phax-plan-extraction answer, whose test lines carry the loop and the technique, move to 0.33.0.

Rename table, test line: loop `oracle` → `acceptance`; `in-phase` unchanged; the fourth field `oracle` keeps its name; a criterion id may be neither `acceptance`, `in-phase` nor `oracle` (`oracle` stays refused so the old loop is recognized and refused by name); technique `boundary` added after `example`. The criterion's reserved words stay a coherence filter, as they have been since 0.32.0, now naming all three: `a criterion is neither 'acceptance', 'in-phase' nor 'oracle'`. The oracle field's three coherence messages keep their wording: they name the fourth field.
Rename table, configuration: key `oracles` → `acceptance` in phax.json, phax.local.json, ~/.phax/config.json and the editor schemas phax.schema.json and phax.user.schema.json.

Rename table, CLI: `--hold oracle` → `--hold acceptance`; `--skip-oracle` → `--skip-acceptance`; "Oracle preflight failed" → "Acceptance preflight failed" (exit 11 unchanged); "The oracle step failed after all fix attempts." → "The acceptance step failed after all fix attempts."; "The oracle step failed after all fix attempts, and protected paths changed." → "The acceptance step failed after all fix attempts, and protected paths changed."; "The protected-path check still runs without the oracle step." → "The protected-path check still runs without the acceptance step."; overview row `oracle role` → `acceptance role` with `acceptance phase, passed by phase-NN` / `passes phase-NN`; records explain row `oracle` → `acceptance` with the same values; `phax plans overview --json` key `oracleRole` → `acceptanceRole`, kind `oracle` with `dischargedBy` → kind `acceptance` with `passedBy`, kind `discharging` with `oraclePhase` → kind `passing` with `acceptancePhase`, kind `none` unchanged.

Rename table, docs and skills: `docs/oracle-phases.md` → `docs/acceptance-phases.md`; site route `/guide/oracle-phases` → `/guide/acceptance-phases`, titled "Acceptance phases"; `examples/vitest-oracles` → `examples/vitest-acceptance`, and this repository's phax.json (`"acceptance": { "command": "node examples/vitest-acceptance/main.mjs" }`) and knip.json follow it. In phax-planning, "What makes a good oracle" becomes "What makes a good acceptance test" and the `#oracle-phases` anchor `#acceptance-phases`. In phax-decide-review, `R4` becomes "Acceptance tests are not fix targets". phax-review says "acceptance pairs", "passed" and "acceptance test" wherever it means a frozen test (its outside-in order, its acceptance-criteria step, its failure modes and its rules), and keeps `wrong-oracle` and the line's fourth field. `site/build/sources.ts` follows the renamed page. The plan-overview page and its site blurb, and the agentic-practices comparison, say acceptance wherever they mean phax's phase, pair or step.

Refusal wording, each normative: `**Oracle phase:** is no longer read: write **Acceptance phase:**`; `**Oracle files:** is no longer read: write **Acceptance test files:**`; `test line <n> uses the loop 'oracle', which is no longer read: write 'acceptance'`; `<file>: "oracles" is no longer read: write "acceptance"`; `--hold 'oracle' is no longer read: write --hold acceptance`; `--skip-oracle is no longer read: write --skip-acceptance`. They follow the existing `**Model reason:** is no longer read: write **Assignment reason:**`.

Every published format whose shape changes is stamped 0.33.0 through `packages/schemas/snapshots/<id>/next.schema.json`, which the 0.33.0 cut renames. Each one's current shape is frozen under `src/schemas/history/<id>/<v>.ts` and pinned in `packages/schemas/history.lock.json`: plan-document 0.32.0, phax-plan 0.32.0, phax-plan-extraction 0.32.0, run-status 0.26.0, phase-status 0.26.0, gate-attribution 0.31.0, phase-record-manifest 0.30.0 and oracle-request 0.26.0. Each stays readable by phax and by the schemas package as it was, `phax-plan-extraction` included, as earlier lifts did, and none is accepted as a current input where a person writes it.

Internal names follow the same table: types, functions, modules, test names and the run preflight check `oracle-phases` (→ `acceptance-phases`) need no row of their own. Only the readers and lifts of earlier shapes, and the frozen schemas of earlier releases, keep the old names.

Answer schemas: the plan authoring and decide-handback answer (plan-document) and the plan-extraction answer carry only the new names, every key required, `$schema` a const of 0.33.0, and still pass the strict check. Claude Code and Codex enforce them while generating. On Mistral Vibe the decoder refuses an old name with the enum's own message and the one corrective resume follows (the extraction fallback has none). No answer refusal names an old name.

The code review's `acceptance` and `boundary` lenses and its `wrong-oracle` escape keep their ids: the code-review answer is not bumped, and compliance-review, which names no oracle phase, is not either.

migrate-documents: the own-shape rendering of a 0.28.0 or 0.32.0 plan sidecar keeps its `**Oracle phase:**` and `**Oracle files:**` lines and its `oracle` loop, so an unedited body is still told apart from an edited one.

Plans: the spec ships as four plans, in this order. (1) Persisted and published formats: the phase key, loop, technique and criterion filter in plan-document, phax-plan and phax-plan-extraction; the status, gate-attribution and record-manifest names; the `acceptance-request` format and its saved file; the schemas package's exports; the frozen modules and lifts; migrate-documents and the extractor version. Covers ac-loop, ac-boundary, ac-criterion, ac-status-record, ac-migrate, ac-unmigrated, ac-archived and ac-in-flight. (2) Lint, CLI and config refusals: the header lines and the `acceptance` lint check, the `tests` loop messages, the `acceptance` config key and its editor schemas, `--hold acceptance`, `--skip-acceptance`, and every old-name refusal. Covers ac-header, ac-header-rules, ac-header-old, ac-loop-rules, ac-loop-old, ac-provider, ac-request-authored, ac-provider-missing, ac-provider-old, ac-hold, ac-hold-old, ac-skip and ac-skip-old. (3) Prompts, messages and telemetry: the phase, fix and authoring prompts, the recovery and resume texts, the help texts and usage contract, the overview, records-explain and review-handoff rows, and the telemetry event. Covers ac-words and ac-read-old. (4) Skills, docs, site and example, run with `phax run --allow-skill-edits`: the four skills, the README, the live docs, the renamed page and route, the renamed example with this repository's phax.json and knip.json, and the 0.33.0 upgrading entry. Covers ac-skill, ac-upgrading and ac-oracle-kept. Plan 4 completes the spec; plans 1 to 3 do not.
open: The exit code of the config, `--hold` and `--skip-oracle` refusals: use the code each command already returns for an invalid configuration or argument.
The wording of the overview, records-explain, recovery and help texts beyond the strings this spec quotes, provided they use only the new terms.
constraints: No back-compat shims: an old name a person writes is refused, never read as an alias. Only records already written and archived artifacts are read in their old shape.
The fourth plan edits the phax-planning skill and its bundled copy, so its runs need `phax run --allow-skill-edits`.
Behaviour of acceptance pairs does not change: every existing oracle-phase test keeps its scenario and asserts the new names.

The decoder and the published JSON Schemas must agree: the technique and loop enums change in the decoder and in the plan-document, phax-plan and phax-plan-extraction schemas. The criterion's reserved words (`acceptance`, `in-phase`, `oracle`) stay a coherence filter, named in those schemas' descriptions. Every changed answer schema still passes the strict check.
An extraction cached by an earlier release is never reused: `EXTRACTOR_VERSION` moves from 4 to 5, as it did when phases gained test lines.

The installed phax that drives these runs (0.32.0 until 0.33.0 is released and installed) reads this repository's phax.json, and runs its `oracles` command, `node examples/vitest-oracles/main.mjs`, in the phase worktree. No phase may leave phax.json, or the example that command runs, in a state that phax refuses. 0.32.0 refuses an `acceptance` key and sends an `oracle-request`, and a build with plan 2 refuses `oracles`. Either the rename keeps the old key and the old request readable while the plans run, or the phax.json and example rename lands only in the last plan, after 0.33.0 is released and installed. Planning chooses. A declared `protectedPaths` list also protects phax.json, so a phase that edits it then fails its gate.
